subject.title: gateway install/status hardcodes ~/Library/LaunchAgents — prevents boot-without-login on macOS

question: Should OpenClaw support a first-class macOS system LaunchDaemon gateway mode, and what explicit scope/privilege contract should install, status, doctor, stop, and uninstall expose?
rationale: This crosses a privileged macOS service boundary: root-owned plist writes/removal, sudo UX, non-root `UserName`, durable environment/TMPDIR handling, and coexistence with user LaunchAgents cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Explicit system scope with safe default
options.body: Keep user LaunchAgent as the default, add an audited opt-in LaunchDaemon scope or guidance flow, and align all service-management surfaces before implementation.

options.title: Diagnostic guidance only
options.body: Do not manage LaunchDaemons from OpenClaw yet; improve status/doctor guidance so headless operators can safely own custom launchd setup themselves.

options.title: Full managed LaunchDaemon mode
options.body: Add first-class LaunchDaemon install/status/start/stop/uninstall support, accepting the larger privileged-service surface after owner review.

recommendation.title: Explicit system scope with safe default
recommendation.body: Keep user LaunchAgent as the default, add an audited opt-in LaunchDaemon scope or guidance flow, and align all service-management surfaces before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal ties steipete to gateway service-management introduction, launchd helpers, and current service command boundaries.
